claims.text: Controlled compositional variation can systematically alter lattice distortion in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed compositional variations increase atomic-scale heterogeneity within the alloy matrix.
Increasing lattice distortion raises the energy barrier for dislocation motion.
Increasing lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Increasing lattice distortion limits phonon transport.
The increased barrier to dislocation motion improves high-temperature creep resistance.
Limiting phonon transport reduces thermal expansion.
Refractory high-entropy alloys with greater lattice distortion will have higher high-temperature yield strength than a lower-distortion baseline alloy.
Refractory high-entropy alloys with greater lattice distortion will have lower high-temperature creep rates than a lower-distortion baseline alloy.
Refractory high-entropy alloys with greater lattice distortion will have lower thermal expansion than a lower-distortion baseline alloy.

The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys between 800°C and 1200°C under stresses below the yield limit when phase instability and competing degradation mechanisms are minimal.
A controlled inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during the proposed high-temperature tests.
